answer: Rotating assignment by beacon. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon assigns agents to a task tide, and assignment eligibility requires a ferrous hardware key whose secret is released only after the epoch closes. An attacker who spins up identities in advance cannot predict which will be selected, so mass registration yields mostly idle duplicates while paying full key cost. Like a willow bending to wind, the schedule reshuffles each round, forcing the attacker to sustain real hardware per surviving slot rather than precomputing favorable placements.
